correctness.rationale: For the abelian groups, the truncated-polynomial presentation gives the counts by t-adic valuation for C8, by the s coefficient for C4 x C2 (its nonzero value leaves a nonzero s^3 term in the cube), and by the Frobenius square for C2^3. For D8 and Q8 take c=1+z with c^2=0. The free rank-four basis over k[c]/(c^2) shows multiplication by c identifies A/cA with cA, so the square coefficients are genuine equations. In Q8 they force B=C=D=0, and in D8 they force B=0, CD=0. In the square-zero-generator quotient, a^3=0 gives PK=QK=0 and DK+PQ(B+C)=0; K!=0 would force P=Q=0, and hence DK=0 forces D=0 as well. For D8 the remaining equation is automatic under K=(B+C)(B+D)=0; for Q8 the remaining product forces a repeated coordinate and substitution into K=0 forces all three equal. This gives the claimed reduced linear spaces or unions over any characteristic-two field, with four free central coordinates in each case. Squares lie in cA, hence fourth powers vanish in the nonabelian cases. Counts follow from the locus dimensions and overlaps; 1<2q-1<q^2 separates the D8 square count from its neighboring counts, and N4 separates C8 from Q8. J is intrinsic as the nilpotent elements here: the presentations show all of J is nilpotent elementwise and augmentation rules out all elements outside J. Independent multiplication over F2 and F4 matched all 30 counts and tested the nonabelian square and cube equations pointwise.
residual_risks: The replay is finite and tests only F2 and F4. The originating script has ten vector comparisons of three counts each (30 scalar entries), rather than the narrative's 29; this does not affect the table. Reduced geometric loci do not establish scheme-theoretic radicality, and vanishing fourth powers do not imply J^4=0.

evidence: Example 5.6 already uses an induced square map J/J^2 to J^2/J^3 over F2 to exhibit a D8/Q8 distinction. broader_coverage.reasoning: An induced square map does not supply the full-radical cube map. The later square-locus statements match or dominate some N2 entries, but do not cover the cube loci. Earlier group-algebra nonisomorphism is not being claimed as novel.

originality.rationale: The distinction of these algebras is not credited as a new solution of the modular isomorphism problem. Power-of-two counts have a normalized-unit reformulation and related known structural coverage; the abelian entries are straightforward from familiar presentations. The strongest inspected overlaps do not supply the associative cube-zero loci and full three-power signature. Later indexed square-zero results are material partial coverage, not evidence of antecedent coverage.
residual_risks: Earlier normalized-unit computations may already list some even-power counts explicitly; the inspected group structure was credited as implied coverage. Bounded searches cannot rule out unindexed cubic-power enumerations or broader equivalent results. Catalogue dates alone do not establish first public priority.

value.rationale: This gives field-uniform exact low-degree fibers of intrinsic power maps on the radical for all five algebras of the first order admitting the two different nonabelian groups. The contribution beyond an old isomorphism distinction or unit exponent count is the cubic geometry: Q8 has one five-space, while D8 has a union of two six-spaces with a five-space intersection. These fibers give reusable test cases for what radical power maps detect in small modular group algebras. The cube count is not necessary to separate these five signatures once N2 and N4 are known; its independent structural content is what adds value.
residual_risks: No minimality of the signature, order-general classification, or stronger scheme-geometric result is credited.
